stem: In a pediatric emergency setting, what is the most common cause of a seemingly high hemoglobin level, often referred to as fictitious polycythemia?
explanation: Loss of fluid volume concentrates the blood cells, causing the hemoglobin measurement to appear elevated until the patient is rehydrated.
rationale: Consider how a loss of body fluids affects the concentration of cells in the bloodstream.

optionExplanations.A: Loss of fluid volume concentrates the blood cells, causing the hemoglobin measurement to appear elevated until the patient is rehydrated.
optionExplanations.B: While hypoxia at high altitudes can drive red cell production, it is categorized as secondary polycythemia rather than fictitious polycythemia.
optionExplanations.C: This is a primary polycythemia involving high production in the bone marrow, which is common in adults but very rare in children.
optionExplanations.D: This condition causes secondary polycythemia due to chronic hypoxia, rather than the temporary concentration of blood seen in dehydration.
